Moving polygon’s vertices draw edge one straight line index space instead, true edge wherever row spacing changes along . Inserting vertex wherever edge crosses wall makes every piece lie within one cell, map exact. Two details. burn’s top row must array’s row 0, fractional array row r (0 south wall first row) becomes y = 300 - r. longitude periodic: polygon crosses grid’s seam 80°E (-280 meets 80) burned lattice two periods wide, stays one piece, columns folded back onto 360 model columns afterwards.
code: ## cut every edge at each wall it crosses; the crossing coordinate is put on ## the wall exactly, and its index is the wall's cut_at_walls <- function(ring, xw, yw) {   pieces <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(ring) - 1L), function(k) {     p <- ring[k, ]; q <- ring[k + 1L, ]     cx <- if (q[1] != p[1]) which(xw > min(p[1], q[1]) & xw < max(p[1], q[1])) else integer()     cy <- if (q[2] != p[2]) which(yw > min(p[2], q[2]) & yw < max(p[2], q[2])) else integer()     t <- c(0, (xw[cx] - p[1]) / (q[1] - p[1]), (yw[cy] - p[2]) / (q[2] - p[2]))     ix <- c(NA, cx - 1, rep(NA, length(cy)))     iy <- c(NA, rep(NA, length(cx)), cy - 1)     o <- order(t)     data.frame(lon = p[1] + t[o] * (q[1] - p[1]), lat = p[2] + t[o] * (q[2] - p[2]),                ix = ix[o], iy = iy[o])   })   out <- do.call(rbind, pieces)   rbind(out, out[1, ]) }  ## longitude and latitude to burn coordinates: x is the (fractional) column, ## y = nrow - r puts array row 0 at the top to_index <- function(pts, xw, yw, nrow) {   x <- stats::approx(xw, seq_along(xw) - 1, pts$lon)$y   r <- stats::approx(yw, seq_along(yw) - 1, pts$lat)$y   x[!is.na(pts$ix)] <- pts$ix[!is.na(pts$ix)]   r[!is.na(pts$iy)] <- pts$iy[!is.na(pts$iy)]   if (anyNA(x) || anyNA(r)) stop("the polygon leaves the rectilinear part of the grid")   cbind(x = x, y = nrow - r) }  ## fold the columns of a burn on a lattice two periods wide back onto one fold_columns <- function(b, ncol) {   r <- b$runs   across <- r$col_start <= ncol & r$col_end > ncol   right <- r[across, ]   right$col_start <- ncol + 1L   r$col_end[across] <- ncol   r <- rbind(r, right)   wrap <- r$col_start > ncol   r$col_start[wrap] <- r$col_start[wrap] - ncol   r$col_end[wrap] <- r$col_end[wrap] - ncol   e <- b$edges   e$col[e$col > ncol] <- e$col[e$col > ncol] - ncol   b$runs <- r[order(r$id, r$row, r$col_start), ]   b$edges <- e   for (nm in c("runs", "edges")) attr(b[[nm]], "row.names") <- .set_row_names(nrow(b[[nm]]))   attr(b, "dimension") <- c(ncol, attr(b, "dimension")[2])   attr(b, "extent") <- c(0, ncol, 0, attr(b, "dimension")[2])   b }  ## burn a polygon given as a closed ring of longitude and latitude (straight ## edges in longitude and latitude, less than 360 degrees wide) burn_lonlat <- function(ring, lon_wall, lat_wall, nrow, cut = TRUE, coverage = TRUE) {   ncol <- length(lon_wall) - 1L   ring[, 1] <- ring[, 1] - 360 * floor((min(ring[, 1]) - lon_wall[1]) / 360)   xw <- c(lon_wall, lon_wall[-1] + 360)   pts <- if (cut) {     cut_at_walls(ring, xw, lat_wall)   } else {     data.frame(lon = ring[, 1], lat = ring[, 2], ix = NA, iy = NA)   }   idx <- to_index(pts, xw, lat_wall, nrow)   g <- wk::wkt(sprintf("POLYGON ((%s))", paste(sprintf("%.17g %.17g", idx[, 1], idx[, 2]), collapse = ", ")))   b <- cb_burn(g, extent = c(0, 2 * ncol, 0, nrow), dimension = c(2 * ncol, nrow), coverage = coverage)   out <- fold_columns(b, ncol)   attr(out, "index_ring") <- idx   out }

text: Take cap cell quadrilateral four corners, straight edged polar stereographic plane. Split four triangles mean corners. quadrilateral triangles opposite sides point hold exactly half area , point inside unit cell splits four triangles shares area. Mapping triangle affinely onto partner gives map plane index space area-proportional within every cell: fraction unit cell fraction quadrilateral. exact curvilinear method crate’s design/grid-frontends.md.
code: ## spherical polar stereographic, the North Pole at the origin stereo <- function(lon, lat) {   rho <- 2 * R * tan(pi / 4 - lat * pi / 360)   cbind(x = rho * sin(lon * pi / 180), y = -rho * cos(lon * pi / 180)) } ## cap cells, array rows 245 to 299 (0-based); the corners of cell (j, i) are ## the corner points (j-1, i-1), (j-1, i), (j, i), (j, i-1), columns periodic cap <- expand.grid(i = 0:359, j = (nrect):299) corner <- function(j, i) stereo(geolon_c[cbind(j + 1, i %% 360 + 1)], geolat_c[cbind(j + 1, i %% 360 + 1)]) SW <- corner(cap$j - 1, cap$i - 1); SE <- corner(cap$j - 1, cap$i) NE <- corner(cap$j, cap$i);         NW <- corner(cap$j, cap$i - 1) M <- (SW + SE + NE + NW) / 4 tri_area <- function(a, b, c) abs((b[, 1] - a[, 1]) * (c[, 2] - a[, 2]) - (c[, 1] - a[, 1]) * (b[, 2] - a[, 2])) / 2 A_b <- tri_area(SW, SE, M); A_r <- tri_area(SE, NE, M); A_t <- tri_area(NE, NW, M); A_l <- tri_area(NW, SW, M) A <- A_b + A_r + A_t + A_l c(cells = nrow(cap), opposite_pairs_off_half = max(abs((A_b + A_t) / A - 0.5), abs((A_l + A_r) / A - 0.5))) #>                   cells opposite_pairs_off_half  #>            1.980000e+04            8.937295e-15  ## each triangle in the plane and its image in index space (x: column, r: array ## row, 0 at the south wall of row 0); the inner point is placed so that every ## triangle keeps its share of the cell's area Mi <- cbind(cap$i + 2 * A_l / A, cap$j + 2 * A_b / A) I_SW <- cbind(cap$i, cap$j); I_SE <- I_SW + rep(c(1, 0), each = nrow(cap)) I_NE <- I_SW + 1;            I_NW <- I_SW + rep(c(0, 1), each = nrow(cap)) tri <- list(p1 = rbind(SW, SE, NE, NW), p2 = rbind(SE, NE, NW, SW), p3 = rbind(M, M, M, M),             q1 = rbind(I_SW, I_SE, I_NE, I_NW), q2 = rbind(I_SE, I_NE, I_NW, I_SW), q3 = rbind(Mi, Mi, Mi, Mi)) tri$bb <- cbind(pmin(tri$p1[, 1], tri$p2[, 1], tri$p3[, 1]), pmax(tri$p1[, 1], tri$p2[, 1], tri$p3[, 1]),                 pmin(tri$p1[, 2], tri$p2[, 2], tri$p3[, 2]), pmax(tri$p1[, 2], tri$p2[, 2], tri$p3[, 2])) tri_edges <- list(a = rbind(tri$p1, tri$p2, tri$p3), b = rbind(tri$p2, tri$p3, tri$p1))

Carried mirrored copy grid top row, (x, r) becoming (360 - x, 600 - r), ring stays one piece; burned taller lattice rows 300 folded back. “chart” (mirrored , shifted whole periods ) changes ring jumps cells neighbours index space.
code: bary <- function(pt, k) {   a <- tri$p1[k, ]; b <- tri$p2[k, ]; c <- tri$p3[k, ]   den <- (b[2] - c[2]) * (a[1] - c[1]) + (c[1] - b[1]) * (a[2] - c[2])   l1 <- ((b[2] - c[2]) * (pt[1] - c[1]) + (c[1] - b[1]) * (pt[2] - c[2])) / den   l2 <- ((c[2] - a[2]) * (pt[1] - c[1]) + (a[1] - c[1]) * (pt[2] - c[2])) / den   c(l1, l2, 1 - l1 - l2) } locate_triangle <- function(pt) {   for (k in which(tri$bb[, 1] <= pt[1] & tri$bb[, 2] >= pt[1] & tri$bb[, 3] <= pt[2] & tri$bb[, 4] >= pt[2])) {     if (all(bary(pt, k) > -1e-9)) return(k)   }   stop("the polygon leaves the cap") } tri_to_index <- function(pt, k) {   l <- bary(pt, k)   l[1] * tri$q1[k, ] + l[2] * tri$q2[k, ] + l[3] * tri$q3[k, ] } ## cut segment p -> q at every triangle edge it crosses cut_at_triangles <- function(p, q) {   lo <- pmin(tri_edges$a, tri_edges$b); hi <- pmax(tri_edges$a, tri_edges$b)   near <- which(hi[, 1] >= min(p[1], q[1]) & lo[, 1] <= max(p[1], q[1]) &                 hi[, 2] >= min(p[2], q[2]) & lo[, 2] <= max(p[2], q[2]))   a <- tri_edges$a[near, , drop = FALSE]; e <- tri_edges$b[near, , drop = FALSE] - a   d <- q - p   den <- d[1] * e[, 2] - d[2] * e[, 1]   t <- ((a[, 1] - p[1]) * e[, 2] - (a[, 2] - p[2]) * e[, 1]) / den   u <- ((a[, 1] - p[1]) * d[2] - (a[, 2] - p[2]) * d[1]) / den   t <- sort(unique(round(t[den != 0 & t > 0 & t < 1 & u >= 0 & u <= 1], 13)))   rbind(p, cbind(p[1] + t * d[1], p[2] + t * d[2])) } ## the fold maps (x, r) to (360 - x, 600 - r); columns repeat every 360 chart <- function(xr, flip, shift) {   if (flip) xr <- cbind(360 - xr[, 1], 600 - xr[, 2])   cbind(xr[, 1] + 360 * shift, xr[, 2]) } ## a closed ring in the stereographic plane to one unbroken ring in index space cap_ring <- function(ring) {   pts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(ring) - 1), function(k) cut_at_triangles(ring[k, ], ring[k + 1, ])))   pts <- rbind(pts, pts[1, ])   out <- NULL; flip <- FALSE; shift <- 0   for (k in seq_len(nrow(pts) - 1)) {     t <- locate_triangle((pts[k, ] + pts[k + 1, ]) / 2)     native <- rbind(tri_to_index(pts[k, ], t), tri_to_index(pts[k + 1, ], t))     seg <- chart(native, flip, shift)     if (!is.null(out) && sum((seg[1, ] - out[nrow(out), ])^2) > 1e-12) {       ## a jump: take the chart that continues the ring       opts <- expand.grid(flip = c(FALSE, TRUE), shift = -2:2)       gap <- mapply(function(f, s) sum((chart(native, f, s)[1, ] - out[nrow(out), ])^2), opts$flip, opts$shift)       if (min(gap) > 1e-8) stop("could not continue the ring across a seam")       flip <- opts$flip[which.min(gap)]; shift <- opts$shift[which.min(gap)]       seg <- chart(native, flip, shift)     }     out <- if (is.null(out)) seg else rbind(out, seg[2, , drop = FALSE])   }   out } ## burn the ring on the unfolded lattice (rows 0 to 600, whole periods of ## columns), then fold it back onto the model's 300 x 360 cells burn_cap <- function(index_ring) {   x0 <- 360 * floor(min(index_ring[, 1]) / 360)   W <- 360 * ceiling((max(index_ring[, 1]) - x0) / 360)   g <- wk::wkt(sprintf("POLYGON ((%s))", paste(sprintf("%.17g %.17g", index_ring[, 1], 600 - index_ring[, 2]),                                                collapse = ", ")))   v <- cb_materialize(cb_burn(g, extent = c(x0, x0 + W, 0, 600), dimension = c(W, 600)), background = 0)   hit <- which(v > 0)   r0 <- (hit - 1) %/% W; c0 <- x0 + (hit - 1) %% W   above <- r0 >= 300   j <- ifelse(above, 599 - r0, r0)   i <- ifelse(above, (359 - c0) %% 360, c0 %% 360)   cov <- numeric(300 * 360)   s <- rowsum(v[hit], j * 360 + i + 1)   cov[as.integer(rownames(s))] <- s[, 1]   cov }
